summary: Elects Ms. Ross, Mr. Ivey, Ms. Garcia of Texas, and Mr. Subramanyam to the House Ethics Committee and Mr. Carter of Louisiana and Mr. Garcia of California to the House Homeland Security Committee.

scores.thoughts: This is a purely procedural House resolution electing members to standing committees. It contains no provisions related to budgets, appropriations, or spending levels of any kind.
The resolution addresses only committee assignments and has no content concerning tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No healthcare policy, coverage, or regulatory provisions appear in the bill text.
The bill is silent on firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
While one committee mentioned is Homeland Security, the resolution itself only names members and does not alter immigration policy or enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
The resolution does not authorize, fund, or modify any military or defense programs.
No environmental or climate-related language is present.
The bill contains nothing regarding welfare programs or social services.
No education policy or funding provisions exist in the text.
The resolution does not engage with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing measures are addressed.
The bill has no connection to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No fiscal policy, deficits, or debt measures are involved.
The resolution does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No foreign aid or international assistance provisions are present.
The bill concerns internal House committee elections only and does not affect public voting access or election procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight language appears.
The resolution does not engage with labor rights, unions, or employment policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
